heading: Strong models can outperform weak supervisors after fine-tuning on their labels
definition: a strong model fine-tuned on a weaker model's labels beats the weak supervisor (performance gap recovered, PGR = (weak-to-strong − weak) / (strong ceiling − weak), above 0).
summary: Several independent groups reproduce gains over weak supervisors across NLP and vision tasks. Gains depend on the task, model pairing and training procedure, with some settings yielding performance at or below the supervisor.

suggested_status.by_scale: Toy/theory: holds only in stated regimes (supporting proofs and simulations; failure regimes are also proven). <1B: R2 but mixed; GPT-2/Pythia pairs split between gains and at-or-below-teacher results. 1-10B: R2, with task-specific challenges (ETHICS-commonsense, SLURP, answer-only labels, Qwen3 reward models). 10-100B: R2 (Qwen-14B, Deepseek 67B and Llama 70B students from several groups). >100B: ?; the original's GPT-4-family sizes are not disclosed, and one gpt-oss-120b study is qualitative. counts: V1.studies_by_size has '1-10B': 36, '10-100B': 14, '<1B': 8, '>100B': 1, 'not stated': 38.
suggested_status.reason:
No tested study shares an author with the original (counts: V1.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original = 0). Key counts: V1.studies_tested = 78; V1.verdicts.supports.studies = 69; V1.verdicts.limits_scope.studies = 46; V1.verdicts.challenges.studies = 29; V1.tested_by_review_class.reviewed = 37; V1.tested_with_uncertainty = 42. Other groups reproduce positive PGR with naive fine-tuning or auxiliary-loss training on the original's kind of binary NLP task, on other families (counts: V1.studies_by_family has Qwen 24, Llama 17, GPT-2 8):
- EleutherAI: Qwen1.5 0.5B to Llama3 8B; default training includes auxiliary log-confidence loss, alpha=.5; PGR > 0 on all 21 non-saturated NLP datasets (web:https://blog.eleuther.ai/weak-to-strong#R1).
- arXiv:2406.03199: Qwen-7B, with SDs.
- arXiv:2501.13124 and arXiv:2511.14166: Qwen-14B.
- arXiv:2503.04249: its Qwen-1.8B to Qwen-14B SciQ PGR (49.5%) is close to arXiv:2511.14166's on the same pair (44.79%).
The challenges are tied to settings: negative naive PGR on ETHICS-commonsense and for Llama3-8B on Hellaswag (arXiv:2406.19032, no uncertainty), SLURP generation, answer-only labels, naive CE on CLIP, small GPT-2 pairs, overtraining, and corruption shift.
suggested_status.open_questions: (1) Do the negative naive PGRs in arXiv:2406.19032 (ETHICS-commonsense; Llama3-8B on Hellaswag) hold with seeds and uncertainty? EleutherAI excluded ETHICS as saturated and found PGR > 0 elsewhere for Llama3 8B. (2) Does a >100B open student fine-tuned on hard weak labels, with a reported ceiling, give PGR > 0? (3) Do <1B GPT-2/Pythia pairs give PGR > 0 beyond noise? arXiv:2402.00667 and arXiv:2505.23933 report at-or-below-teacher or 0% cells, while arXiv:2410.12621 and arXiv:2502.11107 report gains. (4) Do preference-alignment students that start below their supervisor beat it? A failed independent rerun of the original's NLP suite, or evidence that positive PGR comes mainly from saturated or near-chance gaps, would move the level toward C.

source.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization
source.authors: Collin Burns; Pavel Izmailov; J. Kirchner; Bowen Baker; Leo Gao; Leopold Aschenbrenner; Yining Chen; Adrien Ecoffet; Manas R. Joglekar; Jan Leike; I. Sutskever; Jeff Wu

original_result.setup: The study fine-tuned strong GPT-4-family models (students) on labels produced by weaker models (supervisors) for 22 NLP classification datasets, chess puzzles and ChatGPT reward modeling.
original_result.result: Across NLP tasks, students closed more than 20% of the gap between weak-supervisor performance and their own performance with ground-truth training (performance gap recovery), even with very weak supervisors, often exceeding 50% for the largest students. Recovery was usually roughly 10% for reward modeling; in chess, it was near zero with the smallest supervisors but could exceed 40% when supervisor and student were close in size.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: Strong regression students outperformed weak supervisors with every representation tested.

At the selected stopping time, a student with fixed random features far undercut its teacher's loss.
Qwen3-8B students exceeded smaller proxy supervisors on mathematics and code.
Weak demonstrations often led students that hid their abilities to outperform their supervisors.
Two rounds of weak supervision beat the supervisor's recall on hard cases across test models.
Waypoint-OPD distillation students exceeded the 4B teacher on mathematics and code averages.

Direct distillation on student-generated outputs lifted Qwen3-1.7B from below its teacher to above it.

Naive reward-model students exceeded weak supervisors on the specified in-distribution datasets.

Proxy-teacher distillation produced a student exceeding its teacher across three benchmarks.
Contrastive students exceeded weak supervisors aligned with either DPO or ConG.
Synthetic regression students achieved lower error than weak teachers across all six settings.
Trajectory-trained students outperformed weak supervisors, but selection relied on ground-truth rewards from the environment.
Honesty-trained students modestly surpassed Honest-aware Decoding, which selects output tokens, in all six settings.
Qwen2.5 students learning from teacher-scored self-generated outputs peaked above teachers in all ten distillation pairs.
Students exceeded teachers across knowledge, mathematics and chess with naive and trust-function training.
In PCAM's architecture sweep, only ConvNeXt-Base and DenseNet-121 exceeded about 0.84 AUC.

Students closed less of the gap to best performance as weak supervisors fell farther behind.

Students closed less of larger chess gaps and little of reward-modelling gaps to best performance.
Students' error correction varied by class; bag-of-words students copied teacher labels exactly.

Naively fine-tuned Mistral-7B barely exceeded its weak GSM8K supervisor.
SDXL already exceeded SD v2, while weak-data training added little over its baseline.
GPT2-large and GPT2-XL gained little over a GPT2-small teacher without bagging (combining models from resampled data).
With intermediate-strength supervisors, students rarely exceeded imitation training's performance plateau, and only slightly.
Below the study's threshold, student error stayed near chance, like the teacher's.
The ChessFormer 1500 student failed to surpass supervisors; surpassing them required low sampling temperature.
SimPO preference-tuned students did not consistently outperform more capable teachers.

Llama3-70b barely outperformed its weak supervisor on OlympicArena.

Qwen2.5-14B exceeded its reasoning teacher by only about one point on tested math benchmarks.
CLIP students achieved small gains in selected domains and training configurations.
Llama 3 70B barely outperformed its weak GSM8K supervisor, already near the student's best performance.
BoolQ students improved loss but scored below their weak supervisor in accuracy.

BoolQ fine-tuning produced only a small gain over the GPT-2 supervisor.
Training students with fixed random features to convergence erased their advantage over the teacher.
Cell segmentation students showed negligible marker-purity differences and small or absent patch-classification gains.
Wider students gained only within bounded sample-size or feature-count ranges, depending on which resource limited performance.
Answer-only GSM8K students scored far below weak references trained with chain-of-thought labels.
On DROP, DialogSum, and AQuA-RAT, students closed little of the gap to their best performance.
Video-quality students showed negligible in-domain gains even with 200k training videos.
Qwen3-8B still outperformed its weak supervisor after fine-tuning, but scored lower than before fine-tuning.
Students failed to beat an optimally tuned teacher's scaling exponent: how fast performance improves with scale.
In the infinite-data limit, perfectly fitting weak labels yielded the weak model's performance.
Image-generation students mostly trailed supervisors on text-image alignment (CLIP-T), despite small gains in human ratings.
Early pre-training checkpoints failed to outperform the weak supervisor.
In the game Amazons, the student failed to beat its teacher with the smaller search budget.
Plain on-policy math distillation recovered only about 15% of the performance gap.
The tamper-resistant organism matched its supervisor's hard recall at the two-step dose.
On Spider, the student beat its teacher, but variation across random seeds left the gain uncertain.
Continued training erased students' initial gains as they learned to match teacher labels.
Plain on-policy distillation erased the student's initial advantage on AIME 2024.
Code students slightly trailed the 4B-RL (reinforcement learning) teacher, which already outperformed the students' starting model.
A single GPT-2-medium run barely exceeded its GPT-2 supervisor.
Plain on-policy students plateaued near their teachers, with small gains or declines depending on the task.
Across model families, supervised fine-tuning stayed near the supervisor; subsequent direct preference optimization (DPO) exceeded it.
Additional training epochs reduced Pythia and GPT-2 students' gains over weak teachers.
Initial supervised fine-tuning on teacher outputs kept students near the weak teacher's score.
Transformer students did not significantly outperform Snorkel, a weak-supervision system, on query-intent classification.
Plain training on predicted segmentation masks usually underperformed the zero-shot model that supplied them.
Medical-imaging students scored slightly above BiomedCLIP on PCAM, below on ISIC, and nearly equal on NIH.
SLURP students often matched or underperformed weak supervisors across tested supervision variants.
Plain fine-tuning produced students that scored below weak supervisors in tested reasoning and ethics settings.
Tested GPT-2 students generally matched or trailed weak supervisors.
Role-play students trailed supervisors given privileged knowledge on knowledge and rejection evaluations.
The 70B student received lower helpfulness rewards than its smaller supervisors after supervised fine-tuning.
Students trained with Simple Preference Optimization (SimPO) scored below GPT-2-Base and GPT-2-Medium teachers.
Full fine-tuning on weak MATH labels produced a student that scored below its Gemma-2b supervisor.
Regression students could fail when label noise roughly equaled error due to limited model expressiveness.
Students scored below reasoning teachers of similar size on AMC, GPQA, and Minerva.
Several CLIP training configurations tied or underperformed weak supervisors on DomainNet.

GPT2-Medium and GPT2-Large gained nothing over the weak teacher on BoolQ.
Answer-only students trailed weak reference models on TriviaQA and ARC.

With 27k videos, students trained within the task's domain stayed near teachers and usually scored lower.

LlamaGen underperformed its FLUX supervisor on every evaluated metric.

The only >100B student with a V1 verdict (gpt-oss-120b, arXiv:2604.22082) is supported qualitatively, and its numeric rows are normalised to the student's own benign ceiling.

wording_issues.phrase: fine-tuned on a weaker model's labels
wording_issues.issue: Much of the supporting evidence uses other supervision or training. arXiv:2605.05710 trains linear heads on frozen Pythia-6.9B/OLMo-7B backbones. arXiv:2507.06187 uses DPO on weak-over-weaker preference pairs. In arXiv:2402.03749, KD distils teacher predictions, FitNet transfers intermediate features, and AdaptConf combines teacher predictions with student self-supervision. arXiv:2610.21601 uses on-policy transfer of RL-induced teacher policy shifts; weak-label fine-tuning is not evaluated, although the paper supplies no explicit untested-parts list. Pack headers label these recipes 'close' or 'different'.

Supervision need not come from a separate smaller generative model. arXiv:2405.16043 uses deterministic unigram rules; arXiv:2412.03881's WRENCH cases use a Snorkel label model. In 10.18653/v1/2025.findings-acl.529, the weak supervisor is a 3-layer MLP honest head using the target LLM's intermediate representations; pseudo-labels combine head scores with LLM likelihoods. arXiv:2603.08095 trains a Qwen3-4B PRM on majority-voted, answer-informed labels combining a Qwen3-32B judge with MC rollouts. Its comparison against the single judge does not establish superiority over the aggregated labeling supervisor, whose performance is unreported; V1 is therefore undetermined.

wording_issues.phrase: a strong model ... a weaker model
wording_issues.issue: Model size, initial task performance and the strong ceiling differ. arXiv:2505.20072's Qwen2.5-7B(R) teacher beats the vanilla 14B student on every benchmark; on AMC it also exceeds the RL-trained 14B reference, 65.00% versus 60.00%. arXiv:2607.26246's code teacher scores 61.5 versus the student base's 57.6; no strong ceiling or PGR is reported. arXiv:2607.11505's 4B(RL) supervisor (46.5) and Skywork-OR1-Math-7B (45.2) exceed the 8B GRPO reference (44.5). arXiv:2608.20918's xLAM-FC teacher (.8480) exceeds the single-seed gold reference (.8455) and three-seed reference mean (.8460), but lies within its .843–.850 range; its CLINC150 teacher (.9322) exceeds gold references (.9180–.9313). Negative denominators are mathematically defined but unsuitable as positive-gap recovery; beating the initial student alone does not establish a negative denominator.

Supervisor beating can precede training or coexist with declining student performance, so it does not isolate improvement from weak supervision. Tülu-3-8B-SFT starts at 57.2, above supervisors at 55.5 and 45.8 but below the supervisor at 57.5. Qwen3-4B starts at 72.5 versus a 51.3 teacher before Direct-OPD and reaches 77.6; no strong ceiling establishes PGR. After SFT on Qwen3-4B chosen responses, Qwen3-8B scores multi-hop F1 47.8 versus the supervisor's 44.2, below its untuned 50.6. This remains an observed V1 effect because V1 does not require improvement over the student's starting point. A non-sandbagging Qwen3.6-35B-A3B's hard recall falls from its untrained 71.2% to 23.5%, still above the supervisor's 7.8%.

The statement sets no margin or significance test. arXiv:2205.00926 reports .826 versus .822 macro F1, with no significant difference according to the authors. arXiv:2610.21601 reports 56.14 versus 56.13, described as essentially matching, without an uncertainty estimate or significance test. arXiv:2608.20918 reports .7611 versus .7321, with student seeds spanning .7302–.7689. For 27k training videos, arXiv:2505.03631 reports in-domain student-minus-teacher SRCC from -0.004 to +0.002, described as comparable performance without uncertainty estimates. The latter near-ties do not establish statistical noise.

PGR can be unsuitable as positive-gap recovery, extreme or inconsistently computed. arXiv:2406.19032 marks PGR not applicable when weak exceeds ceiling; reversal is established by accuracy instead. For Mistral-7B → Llama3-8B, Hellaswag student/weak/ceiling accuracies are 0.866/0.894/0.891; ETHICS-cm values are 0.669/0.894/0.865. These invalid PGR entries are cannot_determine as PGR measures, while student accuracy is below the supervisor. arXiv:2605.25629 reports PGR 1537.5% (ceiling 88.05, barely above the weak teacher) and -1315.4%. arXiv:2501.13124's Qwen-7B → Qwen-14B AnthropicHH PGR of 35.0% uses weak 48.8 and ceiling 50.8, near chance. arXiv:2410.12621 reports toxicity PGR 0.373, but Eq. 1 gives 0.627.

The statement sets no threshold or uncertainty test, and 'above 0' covers both small and large recovery. Verdicts treat -0.066 ± 0.715 on SLURP as absent, not reversed. PGR is 7.19% for Llama 3 70B on GSM8K but 51.39–65.85% for Deepseek 67B. For 1.7B-to-8B maths, plain OPD scores 28.3 versus supervisor 25.5 and GRPO reference 44.5, with derived PGR approximately 0.147 and partial V1 recovery; P-OPD gives about 0.58. On DomainNet Infograph, AdaptConf+LP accuracy is 33.78% versus weak 31.71%, CE+LP 30.55% and ceiling 50.84%; computed PGR 0.108 is partial V1/V6 recovery, alongside an observed V2 gain. Computed CPL PGR is 0.836 on Clipart, 0.754 on Infograph, 0.899 on Painting and 0.817 on Sketch.

Ceilings are often missing or defined differently. In arXiv:2502.04313 the elicited ceiling is trained on Dtr1, not Dtr2. arXiv:2505.20072's ceiling is an RL-trained student. arXiv:2608.17776 uses an RLVR roofline (0.773). arXiv:2605.05710 trains ceilings but never reports them. Many other studies have no true-label ceiling, so PGR cannot be computed.

Some settings use students other than larger pretrained language models. 173d42ed4cd2dd8e988e628b97727a6c6f52f7a2 uses compact CNNs (DenseNet-121, 8M) under a BiomedCLIP labeller; its PCAM student AUC 0.846 slightly exceeds the approximate teacher ceiling of 0.84, giving partial V1/V6 evidence without reported PGR or a significance test against the teacher. arXiv:2603.10512 uses a custom MCTS/graph framework. arXiv:2603.05691 uses RFRR students.

method_sensitivity.what: Baseline (original): near-universal positive PGR on NLP, PGR close to zero for chess with the smallest supervisors, and usually roughly 10% of the gap for ChatGPT reward modelling. With the same GPT2-Small soft labels, PGR is 0% on BoolQ but 47.00% (GPT2-Medium) and 65.51% (GPT2-Large) on Cosmos QA. With the same Llama2-7B supervisor, the Llama2-13B student gets PGR -2.250 on ETHICS-commonsense but 0.387 on MMLU. Qwen2.5 3B to 7B naive W2S gets PGR -46.24 on AQuA-RAT but 86.34 on GSM8K (text, Table 1).

Going from 1 to 3 epochs moves GPT-2 and Pythia students toward the teacher's accuracy; GPT-2-XL falls below GPT-2-Base's 90.95%, reversing V1 in that condition. Random-feature students reach PGR near 1 with early stopping, but at convergence mimic the teacher with the same error: V1 is absent there. A CNN at nst=20000 is near-perfect in the early phase but ends similar to or below the weak model after overtraining. Linear students' gains peak and then decline. These results demonstrate duration dependence and overtraining failure, rather than reversing those dependence or failure-mode claims.

method_sensitivity.factor: Label format: chain of thought vs answer-only or direct answer
method_sensitivity.what: Qwen2.5-1.5B to 3B on TriviaQA: Q-A gives 30.47 and Q-CoT-A 45.76 versus a separately trained gold-Q-A reference of 32.96. Actual supervisor accuracies are unavailable, so V1 is undetermined. GSM8K's Qwen 1.5B→3B→7B cascade gives 14.18 versus a separate 1.5B gold-CoT reference of 48.18; the final supervisor is 3B. Deepseek 67B CoT PGR is 51.39% on GSM8K and 65.85% on MATH (Tables 8–9). Table 3 reports direct-answer PGR -5.87% and -31.8%; its GSM8K weak/ceiling/student accuracies are 14.6%/30.93%/13.64%. Its caption says Deepseek, but CoT comparator cells match Llama 3, preventing a secure same-model format comparison; the reported MATH PGR is also arithmetically inconsistent.

method_sensitivity.factor: Training objective (naive CE vs confidence losses vs prototypes; auxiliary loss; off-policy SFT vs OPD vs P-OPD)
method_sensitivity.what: CLIP on DomainNet Infograph: CE+LP 30.55%, AuxConf+LP 18.37% and AdaptConf+LP 33.78% versus weak 31.71%; AdaptConf gives partial V1 recovery and improves over CE. CPL PGR is 0.754–0.899 across Clipart, Infograph, Painting and Sketch; naive CE also exceeds weak on Sketch. Adding auxiliary loss moves TinyLlama-supervised SLURP PGR from 0.000 ± 0.084 to -0.250 ± 0.224, while GPT2-Large-supervised SciQ PGR moves from 0.503 to 0.614. Cold-start off-policy SFT on 0.5B-expert rollouts pins students near the teacher without clear superiority; vanilla OPD gives a 14B peak of 77.7% versus teacher 39.8%. Qwen3-1.7B proxy to Qwen3-8B maths: OPD 28.3 versus supervisor 25.5, with verdict-computed PGR approximately 0.147 against GRPO reference 44.5 (partial recovery); P-OPD PGR is about 0.58.

With the same Qwen-14B student on BoolQ, PGR is 3.92% with a GPT-2 supervisor and 17.56% with Qwen-1.8B. With the same Llama2-70b student on MATH, PGR is -25.81 with Gemma-2b versus 10.45 (Llama2-7b) and 19.05 (Mistral-7b). PGR decreases monotonically as the AlexNet supervisor's gap below the 0.74 ceiling widens (figure-only): observed capability-gap dependence, with partial V1 recovery at large gaps. On AdvGLUE++, the Pythia 410M student qualitatively exceeds the unregularized Pythia 14M supervisor's 71% adversarial accuracy (No TFT), but does not surpass the adversarially regularized supervisor's 78% (Weak TFT), leaving V1 absent in that condition.

method_sensitivity.factor: Evaluation metric (loss vs accuracy; PGR normalisation; which quality measure)
method_sensitivity.what: On BoolQ, student heads' test cross-entropy is below the weak model's 0.670, but accuracy is 0.619 and 0.614 versus weak 0.624: V1 reverses on accuracy. PGR becomes extreme when the ceiling barely exceeds weak: 1537.5% (ceiling 88.05) and -1315.4%. Qwen-Chat role-play students exceed supervisors on identity consistency but fall below on knowledge and rejection (figure-only). Autoregressive image students exceed diffusion supervisors on CLIP-I and DINO in seven of eight pairs; LlamaGen/FLUX is below on both. CLIP-T is below in seven of eight pairs. In the human evaluation, Lumina-mGPT/SDXL prompt fidelity is 4.481 versus 4.370.

Reward models, naive: Llama 1B to 8B gives PGR 32–146% across six sources, while Qwen3-1.7B to 8B gives -87.7% on HelpSteer3: reversed V1 but observed family/dataset dependence. method_sensitivity.factor: Data quantity, feature overlap and gold-label budget
method_sensitivity.what: DREAM is the medium-overlap LLM example, performing near or slightly above weak; high-overlap amazon_polarity approaches the strong ceiling (figures). MNIST students score 84.62 at nst=500 versus weak 86.06, but 88.34 at nst=1000 versus weak 85.93. In Case II random-feature regression, positive gain occupies a bounded m interval when samples are the bottleneck; sufficiently large m can help when student width NS is the bottleneck and meets its threshold. At fixed m, width has a bounded feature-bottleneck interval and may have a sample-bottleneck positive half-line. Outside the positive interval on its corresponding bottleneck branch, gain is absent or reversed. PCAM with 50K weak labels: DenseNet-121 AUC is 0.846, 0.851, 0.846, 0.851, 0.844 at ng=10,20,50,100,500 versus gold-only 0.579,0.662,0.832,0.868,0.922. These are small positive differences from approximate teacher AUC 0.84: partial V1 recovery, without reported PGR or teacher-comparison significance.

method_sensitivity.factor: Search budget and regularization tuning (analogue settings)
method_sensitivity.what: The Amazons analogue's win rate against GPT-4o-mini is 45.0% at N=30 and 66.5% at N=50; stronger pretrained capability recovery and PGR are untested. In RFRR, the student's scaling exponent improves only when the teacher is sub-optimally tuned; with both optimally tuned, the exponents are equal. Equal exponents do not determine V1 superiority because a constant-factor performance advantage remains possible. The tuning dependence and theoretical exponent boundary are established.
